_comment: Mi'yar — CEFR grammar syllabus. Per-level ordered grammar points (week, cefr, title, EN/AR explanation, examples), authored against public English Grammar Profile A1 concepts. One point per week; the week file references it by week number.

A1.title: Verb 'to be' + subject pronouns
A1.en: Use am / is / are with I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Make simple statements and yes/no questions about identity and origin.
A1.ar: استخدام am / is / are مع الضمائر. جمل بسيطة وأسئلة نعم/لا عن الهوية والأصل.
examples: I am from Egypt.
She is a student.
Are you a teacher?
They are my friends.

A1.title: Possessive adjectives + 'have got'
A1.en: my, your, his, her, our, their. Talk about family and belongings with have got / has got.
A1.ar: صفات الملكية (my, your, his...) والكلام عن العائلة والممتلكات بـ have got.
examples: This is my sister.
He has got two brothers.
Their house is big.

A1.title: Numbers, 'there is/are' + time prepositions (at/in/on)
A1.en: Cardinal numbers, there is / there are for existence, and at/in/on for times and days.
A1.ar: الأرقام، there is/are للوجود، وحروف الوقت at/in/on.
examples: There are seven days in a week.
The class is at three o'clock.
My birthday is in June.
I work on Monday.

A1.title: Place prepositions + 'this/that/these/those'
A1.en: in, on, under, next to, behind, between; and demonstratives this/that/these/those.
A1.ar: حروف المكان (in, on, under...) وأسماء الإشارة this/that/these/those.
examples: The book is on the table.
This is my room.
Those are my shoes.

A1.title: Present simple (I/you/we/they)
A1.en: Everyday routines and habits with the base verb for I/you/we/they, plus negatives with don't.
A1.ar: المضارع البسيط للروتين اليومي مع I/you/we/they، والنفي بـ don't.
examples: I get up at seven.
We eat breakfast together.
They don't work on Friday.

A1.title: Present simple (he/she/it) -s + some/any
A1.en: Third-person -s, questions with does, and some/any with countable/uncountable food words.
A1.ar: إضافة -s للغائب المفرد، أسئلة بـ does، و some/any مع الأكل.
examples: She likes tea.
Does he eat meat?
We have some bread.
There isn't any milk.

A1.title: 'How much / how many' + shopping language
A1.en: Ask about price and quantity: how much is…?, how many…?, I'd like…, and prices/money.
A1.ar: السؤال عن السعر والكمية: how much/how many، I'd like، والأسعار.
examples: How much is this?
How many apples?
I'd like two, please.

A1.title: Adjectives + describing people and things
A1.en: Common adjectives before nouns and after 'be'; question words what/who/where/how.
A1.ar: الصفات قبل الأسماء وبعد be؛ وأدوات السؤال what/who/where/how.
examples: She has long hair.
The car is fast.
What is he like?
Where is she from?

A1.title: 'can/can't' (ability) + like/love + -ing
A1.en: Express ability with can/can't and preferences with like/love/hate + verb-ing.
A1.ar: التعبير عن القدرة بـ can/can't والتفضيلات بـ like/love + الفعل+ing.
examples: I can swim.
He can't drive.
She likes reading.
We love playing football.

A1.title: Past of 'to be' (was/were) + review
A1.en: Talk about the past with was/were; consolidate all A1 grammar in short personal accounts.
A1.ar: الكلام عن الماضي بـ was/were؛ ومراجعة كل قواعد A1 في جمل شخصية قصيرة.
examples: I was at home yesterday.
They were happy.
Where were you?

A2.title: Past simple — regular verbs (-ed)
A2.en: Talk about finished past actions with regular -ed verbs; time expressions (yesterday, last week, ago).
A2.ar: الكلام عن أحداث ماضية منتهية بالأفعال المنتظمة (-ed) وتعبيرات الوقت (yesterday, last week, ago).
examples: I watched a film yesterday.
We played football last week.
She worked late.

A2.title: Past simple — irregular verbs + did/didn't questions & negatives
A2.en: Common irregular past forms (went, saw, had, made) and questions/negatives with did / didn't.
A2.ar: الأفعال الشاذة في الماضي (went, saw, had) والأسئلة والنفي بـ did / didn't.
examples: I went to Cairo.
Did you see him?
They didn't come.

A2.title: Comparative adjectives (-er / more … than)
A2.en: Compare two things with -er than for short adjectives and more … than for longer ones.
A2.ar: المقارنة بين شيئين بـ -er than للصفات القصيرة و more … than للصفات الطويلة.
examples: Cairo is bigger than Aswan.
This book is more interesting than that one.
She is taller than me.

A2.title: Superlative adjectives (the -est / the most)
A2.en: Say which is the most in a group with the -est / the most, plus one of the + superlative.
A2.ar: التعبير عن الأعلى في مجموعة بـ the -est / the most.
examples: It is the biggest city.
This is the most beautiful place.
He is one of the best players.

A2.title: Future: 'be going to' (plans and intentions)
A2.en: Talk about plans and intentions already decided with be going to + base verb.
A2.ar: الكلام عن الخطط والنوايا المقررة بـ be going to + الفعل.
examples: I'm going to visit my family.
We're going to travel in summer.
Are you going to study tonight?

A2.title: Future: 'will' (decisions, predictions, offers)
A2.en: Use will for on-the-spot decisions, predictions and offers; won't for the negative.
A2.ar: استخدام will للقرارات اللحظية والتوقعات والعروض؛ و won't للنفي.
examples: I think it will rain.
I'll help you.
She won't be late.

A2.title: Present continuous (now) vs present simple
A2.en: Contrast actions happening now (am/is/are + -ing) with habits and routines (present simple).
A2.ar: الفرق بين الأحداث اللي بتحصل دلوقتي (am/is/are + -ing) والعادات (المضارع البسيط).
examples: I usually walk, but today I'm taking the bus.
She is cooking now.
What are you doing?

A2.title: Countable/uncountable + quantifiers (much/many/a lot of/a few/a little)
A2.en: Use much/many, a lot of, a few, a little with countable and uncountable nouns; how much/how many.
A2.ar: استخدام much/many و a lot of و a few و a little مع المعدود وغير المعدود.
examples: There isn't much sugar.
I have a few friends.
How many eggs do we need?

A2.title: Adverbs of manner (well, quickly, carefully)
A2.en: Describe how actions are done with adverbs of manner; regular -ly and irregular (good→well).
A2.ar: وصف طريقة أداء الفعل بظروف الحال (-ly والشاذ good→well).
examples: She speaks English well.
He drives carefully.
Please walk quickly.

A2.title: Present perfect for experience (ever / never, been)
A2.en: Talk about life experience without a specific time using have/has + past participle; ever/never; been to.
A2.ar: الكلام عن الخبرات الحياتية بدون وقت محدد بـ have/has + التصريف الثالث؛ ever/never؛ been to.
examples: Have you ever been to London?
I have never eaten sushi.
She has been to three countries.

A2.title: Obligation & advice: have to / must / should
A2.en: Express necessity with have to / must, absence of obligation with don't have to, and advice with should.
A2.ar: التعبير عن الضرورة بـ have to / must، وغياب الإلزام بـ don't have to، والنصيحة بـ should.
examples: I have to work tomorrow.
You must wear a seatbelt.
You should see a doctor.
We don't have to hurry.

A2.title: Connectors + review (because, so, but, when, before/after)
A2.en: Link ideas into longer sentences with because, so, but, when, before/after; consolidate all A2 grammar.
A2.ar: ربط الأفكار في جمل أطول بـ because وso وbut وwhen؛ ومراجعة كل قواعد A2.
examples: I stayed home because I was tired.
It was late, so we left.
I called when I arrived.

B1.title: Present perfect vs past simple (for/since, already/yet/just)
B1.en: Contrast finished past (past simple) with experience/unfinished time (present perfect); for/since, already/yet/just.
B1.ar: الفرق بين الماضي المنتهي (past simple) والخبرة/الزمن غير المنتهي (present perfect)؛ for/since وalready/yet/just.
examples: I have lived here since 2020.
She has just arrived.
Have you finished yet?
I saw that film last week.

B1.title: Past continuous + past simple (when / while)
B1.en: Background action in progress (was/were + -ing) interrupted by a completed action; when vs while.
B1.ar: حدث مستمر في الخلفية (was/were + -ing) قاطعه حدث منتهٍ؛ when مقابل while.
examples: I was cooking when the phone rang.
While we were talking, it started to rain.
They were sleeping at midnight.

B1.title: Future forms: will vs going to vs present continuous
B1.en: Choose between predictions/decisions (will), plans/intentions (going to) and fixed arrangements (present continuous).
B1.ar: الاختيار بين التوقعات/القرارات (will) والخطط (going to) والترتيبات المؤكدة (present continuous).
examples: I'm meeting Sara at 6 tomorrow.
I think it will be fine.
We're going to move next year.

B1.title: First conditional + time clauses (when/as soon as/unless)
B1.en: Real future conditions: if + present, will; and future time clauses with when/as soon as/unless.
B1.ar: الشرط الحقيقي للمستقبل: if + مضارع، will؛ وجُمَل الزمن المستقبلية بـ when/as soon as/unless.
examples: If it rains, we'll stay home.
I'll call you when I arrive.
Unless you hurry, you'll be late.

B1.title: Second conditional (if + past, would)
B1.en: Hypothetical/unreal present or future: if + past simple, would + base verb.
B1.ar: الافتراض غير الواقعي في الحاضر/المستقبل: if + ماضٍ بسيط، would + الفعل.
examples: If I had more time, I would travel.
What would you do if you won?
I wouldn't say that if I were you.

B1.title: Modals of deduction & possibility (must / might / could / can't)
B1.en: Degrees of certainty about the present: must (sure), might/may/could (possible), can't (impossible).
B1.ar: درجات اليقين عن الحاضر: must (متأكد)، might/may/could (ممكن)، can't (مستحيل).
examples: He must be tired.
She might be at work.
That can't be right.
It could be true.

B1.title: Present perfect continuous (how long, for/since)
B1.en: Recent or ongoing activity emphasising duration: have/has been + -ing; how long, for/since.
B1.ar: نشاط مستمر أو حديث مع التركيز على المدة: have/has been + -ing؛ how long وfor/since.
examples: I've been studying for three hours.
How long have you been waiting?
She's been living here since May.

B1.title: used to / would (past habits and states)
B1.en: Talk about past habits and states that are no longer true with used to; would for repeated past actions.
B1.ar: الكلام عن عادات وحالات ماضية لم تعد قائمة بـ used to؛ وwould للأفعال المتكررة في الماضي.
examples: I used to play football every day.
We would visit my grandmother every summer.
There used to be a cinema here.

B1.title: Comparatives & superlatives (advanced: as…as, much/far, the …the)
B1.en: Refine comparisons: (not) as … as, much/far + comparative, and the + comparative, the + comparative.
B1.ar: تحسين المقارنات: (not) as … as، وmuch/far + المقارنة، وthe + مقارنة، the + مقارنة.
examples: It's not as expensive as I thought.
This is far better.
The more you practise, the better you get.

B1.title: Relative clauses (who / which / that / where / whose)
B1.en: Add information about people, things and places with defining relative clauses.
B1.ar: إضافة معلومات عن الأشخاص والأشياء والأماكن بجُمَل الوصل التعريفية.
examples: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
This is the book that I told you about.
That's the café where we met.

B1.title: Reported speech (statements + say/tell)
B1.en: Report what someone said, shifting tense back one step; say vs tell.
B1.ar: نقل ما قاله شخص مع تراجع الزمن خطوة؛ الفرق بين say وtell.
examples: He said he was tired.
She told me she had finished.
They said they would come.

B1.title: The passive (present & past simple)
B1.en: Focus on the action/result rather than the doer: am/is/are + past participle; was/were + past participle; by + agent.
B1.ar: التركيز على الفعل/النتيجة بدل الفاعل: am/is/are + التصريف الثالث؛ was/were + التصريف الثالث؛ by + الفاعل.
examples: Coffee is grown in Brazil.
The bridge was built in 1990.
This song was written by my friend.

B1.title: Quantifiers & degree (too / enough, both/neither/either, a bit/a lot)
B1.en: Express quantity and degree precisely: too + adj, adj + enough, both/neither/either, a bit/a lot.
B1.ar: التعبير الدقيق عن الكمية والدرجة: too + صفة، صفة + enough، both/neither/either، a bit/a lot.
examples: It's too expensive.
She isn't old enough.
Neither option is good.
I'm a bit tired.

B1.title: Gerunds & infinitives + linkers (although/however/so that) + review
B1.en: Verb + -ing vs verb + to; and link ideas with although, however, because of, so that; consolidate all B1.
B1.ar: الفعل + -ing مقابل الفعل + to؛ وربط الأفكار بـ although وhowever وbecause of وso that؛ ومراجعة كل B1.
examples: I enjoy reading.
I want to travel.
Although it was hard, I finished.
I saved money so that I could travel.

B2.title: Present perfect simple vs continuous (refined)
B2.en: Contrast completed results (simple) with ongoing/temporary activity and duration (continuous) in nuanced cases.
B2.ar: الفرق الدقيق بين النتيجة المكتملة (البسيط) والنشاط المستمر/المؤقت والمدة (المستمر).
examples: I've written three reports today.
I've been writing reports all day.
She's cut her hair.
She's been cutting the grass.

B2.title: Past perfect (simple & continuous)
B2.en: Show an earlier past before another past action; had done vs had been doing.
B2.ar: التعبير عن ماضٍ أسبق من ماضٍ آخر؛ had done مقابل had been doing.
examples: When I arrived, they had already left.
I was tired because I had been working.
She had never seen snow before.

B2.title: Narrative tenses together (past simple/continuous/perfect)
B2.en: Combine past tenses to sequence events, background and earlier events in a story.
B2.ar: الجمع بين أزمنة الماضي لترتيب الأحداث والخلفية والأحداث الأسبق في السرد.
examples: I was walking home when I realised I had forgotten my keys.
By the time we arrived, the film had started.

B2.title: Future perfect & future continuous
B2.en: will have done (completed before a future point) and will be doing (in progress at a future time).
B2.ar: will have done (منتهٍ قبل نقطة مستقبلية) و will be doing (مستمر في وقت مستقبلي).
examples: By 2030 I will have graduated.
This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Cairo.
They'll have finished by noon.

B2.title: Third conditional (if + past perfect, would have)
B2.en: Talk about unreal/imagined past and its imagined result: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
B2.ar: الحديث عن ماضٍ غير واقعي ونتيجته المتخيّلة: if + past perfect، would have + التصريف الثالث.
examples: If I had studied, I would have passed.
She wouldn't have missed it if she'd left earlier.

B2.title: Mixed conditionals
B2.en: Mix time frames: past condition → present result, and present condition → past result.
B2.ar: خلط الأزمنة: شرط ماضٍ ← نتيجة حاضرة، وشرط حاضر ← نتيجة ماضية.
examples: If I had saved money, I would be rich now.
If I were more careful, I wouldn't have made that mistake.

B2.title: wish / if only (regrets & wishes)
B2.en: Express wishes and regrets about the present (wish + past) and past (wish + past perfect); wish + would for complaints.
B2.ar: التعبير عن الأمنيات والندم عن الحاضر (wish + ماضٍ) والماضي (wish + past perfect)؛ wish + would للشكوى.
examples: I wish I had more time.
I wish I had studied harder.
I wish it would stop raining.

B2.title: Reported speech (questions, commands, requests + reporting verbs)
B2.en: Report questions, orders and requests; use reporting verbs (advise, warn, offer, suggest, admit).
B2.ar: نقل الأسئلة والأوامر والطلبات؛ واستخدام أفعال النقل (advise, warn, offer, suggest, admit).
examples: She asked where I lived.
He told me to wait.
They advised us to book early.
He admitted breaking it.

B2.title: Passive (all tenses) + causative have/get something done
B2.en: Use the passive across tenses and with modals; and have/get something done for services.
B2.ar: استخدام المبني للمجهول عبر الأزمنة ومع الأفعال الناقصة؛ و have/get something done للخدمات.
examples: The road is being repaired.
It should have been checked.
I had my car repaired.
We're getting the house painted.

B2.title: Modals of past deduction (must/might/could/can't have + done)
B2.en: Make deductions about the past: must have (certain), might/could have (possible), can't have (impossible).
B2.ar: استنتاجات عن الماضي: must have (متأكد)، might/could have (ممكن)، can't have (مستحيل).
examples: He must have left already.
She might have forgotten.
They can't have finished so fast.

B2.title: Relative clauses: non-defining & reduced
B2.en: Add extra (non-essential) information with non-defining clauses (commas); and reduce relatives to participles.
B2.ar: إضافة معلومات إضافية بجُمَل الوصل غير التعريفية (بفواصل)؛ واختصار جُمَل الوصل إلى مشتقّات.
examples: My boss, who is very kind, helped me.
Cairo, which is huge, is the capital.
The man sitting there is my uncle.

B2.title: Gerunds & infinitives (advanced verb patterns + meaning change)
B2.en: Master verb patterns and verbs where -ing vs to changes meaning (remember, stop, try, regret, go on).
B2.ar: إتقان أنماط الأفعال والأفعال اللي يتغيّر معناها بين -ing و to (remember, stop, try, regret).
examples: I stopped smoking.
I stopped to smoke.
Remember to lock the door.
I remember locking it.

B2.title: Determiners, articles & quantifiers (advanced)
B2.en: Refine article use and generalisations; quantifiers all/most/none of, each/every, both/either/neither.
B2.ar: تدقيق استخدام أدوات التعريف والتعميم؛ ومحدّدات الكمية all/most/none of، each/every.
examples: Most people agree.
Most of the students passed.
Neither of them came.
Each answer counts.

B2.title: Linking & discourse: contrast, concession, cause & result
B2.en: Connect ideas formally: despite/in spite of, although/even though, however/nevertheless, therefore/as a result.
B2.ar: ربط الأفكار بشكل رسمي: despite/in spite of، although/even though، however/nevertheless، therefore.
examples: Despite the rain, we went out.
Even though it was hard, she succeeded.
The demand rose; therefore, prices increased.

B2.title: Emphasis: cleft sentences (It was… that / What… is) + so/such … that
B2.en: Add emphasis with cleft sentences (It was… that; What I need is…) and so/such … that.
B2.ar: إضافة التوكيد بالجُمَل المشقوقة (It was… that؛ What I need is…) و so/such … that.
examples: It was Sara who called.
What I really need is time.
It was so cold that we stayed in.
She had such a busy day that she slept early.

B2.title: Phrasal verbs, collocations & register + review
B2.en: Use common phrasal verbs and collocations, and adjust register (formal vs informal); consolidate all B2.
B2.ar: استخدام الأفعال المركّبة والمتلازمات اللفظية، وضبط الأسلوب (رسمي مقابل غير رسمي)؛ ومراجعة كل B2.
examples: The meeting was called off.
I'd like to bring up a point.
make a decision, take responsibility.
I look forward to hearing from you.

C1.title: Inversion after negative/limiting adverbials
C1.en: Front a negative/limiting adverbial and invert subject–auxiliary for emphasis (Never, Rarely, Seldom, Not only, No sooner … than, Little).
C1.ar: تقديم ظرف نفي/تحديد مع قلب الفاعل والفعل المساعد للتوكيد (Never, Rarely, Not only, No sooner…than).
examples: Never have I seen such a thing.
Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.
No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain.
Rarely do we get such a chance.

C1.title: Inversion in conditionals (Had I / Were I / Should you)
C1.en: Formal conditionals without 'if' via inversion: Had I known…, Were I to…, Should you need….
C1.ar: الشرط الرسمي بدون 'if' عبر القلب: Had I known…، Were I to…، Should you need….
examples: Had I known, I would have helped.
Were I to accept, I'd start Monday.
Should you need anything, let me know.

C1.title: Advanced cleft sentences & fronting
C1.en: Rearrange for emphasis and information flow: cleft (It is… that; What/All/The thing… is) and fronting of objects/complements.
C1.ar: إعادة الترتيب للتوكيد وتدفّق المعلومة: الجُمَل المشقوقة وتقديم المفعول/المكمّل.
examples: It was her patience that impressed me.
What he needs is time.
That I can't accept.
The one thing I regret is leaving.

C1.title: Participle clauses (present, past, perfect)
C1.en: Reduce clauses to participles for concise, formal style: Having finished…, Seen from above…, Being aware….
C1.ar: اختصار الجُمَل إلى مشتقّات لأسلوب موجز ورسمي: Having finished…، Being aware….
examples: Having finished the report, she left.
Seen from above, the city looks tiny.
Not knowing the way, we asked.

C1.title: Advanced & impersonal passive (it is thought that…)
C1.en: Impersonal reporting passives and passive infinitives: It is believed that…; He is thought to have left; is said to be.
C1.ar: المبني للمجهول غير الشخصي وأفعال النقل: It is believed that…؛ He is thought to have left.
examples: It is widely believed that prices will rise.
He is thought to have acted alone.
The scheme is said to be effective.

C1.title: Nominalisation (verbs/adjectives → nouns) for formal register
C1.en: Turn actions and qualities into noun phrases for academic register: 'prices rose' → 'the rise in prices'.
C1.ar: تحويل الأفعال والصفات إلى عبارات اسمية للأسلوب الأكاديمي: 'prices rose' ← 'the rise in prices'.
examples: The introduction of the policy caused concern.
Her refusal surprised us.
There was a significant improvement in results.

C1.title: Advanced modals & semi-modals
C1.en: Nuanced modality: needn't have, was/were to have, be bound/likely to, may well, might as well, would rather.
C1.ar: دلالات دقيقة للأفعال الناقصة: needn't have، be bound to، may well، would rather.
examples: You needn't have worried.
They were to have met yesterday.
It may well be true.
We might as well start.

C1.title: Hedging & cautious language
C1.en: Soften and qualify claims: tend to, appear/seem to, it would seem, arguably, to some extent, by and large.
C1.ar: تخفيف وتقييد الادّعاءات: tend to، appear to، it would seem، arguably، to some extent.
examples: This would appear to suggest a link.
It is, arguably, the best option.
The data tend to support this.

C1.title: Advanced discourse markers & cohesion
C1.en: Signal complex relationships formally: hence, thereby, conversely, notwithstanding, in that, insofar as.
C1.ar: الإشارة للعلاقات المعقّدة رسميًا: hence، thereby، conversely، notwithstanding، insofar as.
examples: Costs fell; hence, margins improved.
It is efficient in that it saves time.
Notwithstanding the risks, they proceeded.

C1.title: Relative clauses (quantifier + which/whom; prepositional)
C1.en: Precise, formal relatives: many of which, most of whom, the extent to which, a point at which.
C1.ar: جُمَل وصل دقيقة ورسمية: many of which، most of whom، the extent to which.
examples: The reports, most of which were positive, were published.
The degree to which this matters is unclear.
It is a stage at which mistakes are common.

C1.title: Ellipsis & substitution
C1.en: Avoid repetition efficiently with ellipsis and substitute forms: so/neither do I, one/ones, do so, if not.
C1.ar: تجنّب التكرار بكفاءة عبر الحذف والاستبدال: so/neither do I، one/ones، do so.
examples: I finished, but she didn't.
So do I.
I need a pen — the blue one.
He promised to help, and he did so.

C1.title: Emphasis & intensification
C1.en: Add emphasis with auxiliary 'do', and intensifiers: far too, nowhere near, by far, all the more, utterly.
C1.ar: التوكيد بـ 'do' المساعدة، والمكثّفات: far too، nowhere near، by far، utterly.
examples: I do appreciate your help.
It's far too expensive.
This is by far the best.
That makes it all the more impressive.

C1.title: Future in the past & complex time reference
C1.en: Refer to a future seen from the past and layered time: was going to, would later, was to become, by which time.
C1.ar: الإشارة لمستقبل من منظور الماضي وزمن متعدّد الطبقات: was going to، would later، by which time.
examples: I was going to call, but forgot.
She would later regret it.
He was to become a leader.
By the time we knew, it was too late.

C1.title: Advanced conditionals (provided/as long as/supposing; inverted)
C1.en: Nuanced conditions with provided (that), as long as, unless, supposing, on condition that; and inverted conditionals.
C1.ar: شروط دقيقة بـ provided that، as long as، unless، supposing، on condition that؛ والشرط المقلوب.
examples: Provided that you're careful, it's safe.
I'll go as long as you come.
Supposing it fails, what then?
Had they invested, they'd have profited.

C1.title: Idiomatic & figurative language + deep collocation
C1.en: Understand and use idioms, metaphor and strong collocations naturally and appropriately.
C1.ar: فهم واستخدام التعابير الاصطلاحية والمجاز والمتلازمات القوية بشكل طبيعي ومناسب.
examples: It's a grey area.
That's a stretch.
to shed light on an issue
a far-reaching decision

C1.title: Register & style shifting
C1.en: Move deliberately between academic, journalistic, professional and conversational registers.
C1.ar: التنقّل المتعمّد بين الأساليب الأكاديمية والصحفية والمهنية والمحادثة.
examples: formal: 'We regret to inform you…' / informal: 'Sorry, but…'
'commence' vs 'start'
'a substantial number' vs 'loads'

C1.title: Complex noun phrases & precision
C1.en: Pack meaning into pre- and post-modified noun phrases for precise, economical expression.
C1.ar: تكثيف المعنى في عبارات اسمية مركّبة (تعديل قبلي وبعدي) لتعبير دقيق واقتصادي.
examples: a rapidly growing, export-driven economy
the recently announced government proposals
concerns about the long-term impact of the policy

C1.title: Fluency, coherence & discourse strategies + review
C1.en: Sustain coherent, well-organised extended discourse; paraphrase, self-correct smoothly, and hold the floor; consolidate all C1.
C1.ar: الحفاظ على خطاب مطوّل متماسك ومنظّم؛ إعادة الصياغة والتصحيح الذاتي بسلاسة؛ ومراجعة كل C1.
examples: What I'm trying to say is…
To put it another way…
Let me come back to that.
As I was saying…

C2.title: The formal & formulaic subjunctive
C2.en: Mandative subjunctive after verbs/adjectives of demand and fixed subjunctive expressions: I insist that he be present; It is essential that it remain; be that as it may; suffice it to say.
C2.ar: صيغة الشرط الرسمية بعد أفعال/صفات الطلب، والعبارات الشرطية الثابتة: I insist that he be present؛ be that as it may؛ suffice it to say.
examples: It is essential that every member be informed.
I demand that he apologise.
Be that as it may, we must proceed.
Suffice it to say, the plan failed.

C2.title: Literary conditionals: 'were it not for' / 'had it not been for'
C2.en: Formal, marked conditional structures beyond C1: Were it not for…, Had it not been for…, But for…, Should the need arise.
C2.ar: تراكيب شرطية رسمية ومميّزة تتجاوز C1: Were it not for…، Had it not been for…، But for…، Should the need arise.
examples: Were it not for your help, I would have failed.
Had it not been for the delay, we'd have arrived.
But for a single vote, the motion would have passed.
Should the need arise, we will act.

C2.title: Stylistic inversion & marked word order for effect
C2.en: Deliberate inversion and fronting for rhetorical and literary effect beyond standard adverbial inversion: So great was the demand…; Such was the response…; Down came the rain.
C2.ar: القلب والتقديم المتعمّد للأثر البلاغي والأدبي بما يتجاوز القلب الظرفي المعتاد: So great was…؛ Such was…؛ Down came the rain.
examples: So great was the demand that stocks ran out.
Such was her influence that all agreed.
Down came the rain, and up went the umbrellas.
Only later did the truth emerge.

C2.title: Advanced fronting & information packaging (theme/rheme)
C2.en: Control end-weight, end-focus and thematic fronting to manage information flow and emphasis across a text.
C2.ar: التحكّم في الثقل النهائي والتركيز النهائي والتقديم الموضوعي لإدارة تدفّق المعلومة والتوكيد عبر النصّ.
examples: This point I shall return to later.
What matters most is trust.
Into the room walked the director.
Of the many options, one stands out.

C2.title: Cleft mastery (it-cleft, wh-cleft, all-cleft, there-cleft)
C2.en: Full command of all cleft types to package and emphasise information precisely: It was… that; What… is; All… is; The reason… is; There is… that.
C2.ar: إتقان كامل لكل أنواع الجُمَل المشقوقة لتغليف المعلومة وتوكيدها بدقّة: It was… that؛ What… is؛ All… is؛ The reason… is.
examples: It was patience that won the day.
What we need is clarity.
All I ask is honesty.
The reason it failed is cost.
There was one thing that troubled me.

C2.title: Grammatical metaphor & extreme nominalisation
C2.en: Compress whole clauses into dense abstract noun phrases for high academic register (grammatical metaphor): 'because prices rose, sales fell' → 'the rise in prices led to a fall in sales'.
C2.ar: ضغط جُمَل كاملة في عبارات اسمية مجرّدة كثيفة للأسلوب الأكاديمي العالي (الاستعارة النحوية).
examples: The rapid deterioration in conditions prompted intervention.
Her early departure occasioned much comment.
The failure of negotiations led to escalation.
Widespread adoption drove the reduction in cost.

C2.title: Advanced concessive & universal-conditional structures
C2.en: Sophisticated concession and unconditionals: much as, for all, however + adjective, whatever/whoever/wherever, albeit, notwithstanding that.
C2.ar: تراكيب التنازل والشرط الشامل الراقية: much as، for all، however + صفة، whatever/whoever، albeit.
examples: Much as I admire her, I disagree.
For all his wealth, he is unhappy.
However hard it seems, persist.
Albeit costly, the plan is sound.

C2.title: Meta-discourse & sophisticated cohesion
C2.en: Signal your own discourse and guide the reader: as noted above, it is worth stressing, to digress briefly, by way of illustration, in parenthesis.
C2.ar: الإشارة إلى خطابك وتوجيه القارئ: as noted above، it is worth stressing، by way of illustration، in parenthesis.
examples: As noted above, the trend is clear.
It is worth stressing one caveat.
By way of illustration, consider this.
To digress briefly, the origin is older.

C2.title: Epistemic stance & evidentiality (mastery)
C2.en: Signal the source and strength of knowledge precisely: it stands to reason, by all accounts, to the best of my knowledge, if anything, in all likelihood.
C2.ar: الإشارة بدقّة إلى مصدر المعرفة وقوّتها: it stands to reason، by all accounts، to the best of my knowledge، if anything، in all likelihood.
examples: By all accounts, it succeeded.
It stands to reason that costs will rise.
To the best of my knowledge, no one objected.
If anything, the problem is worse.

C2.title: Near-synonym discrimination & precise lexical choice
C2.en: Choose the exact word among close synonyms, controlling collocation and shade of meaning: dispute/contest/refute; big/substantial/considerable; end/terminate/conclude.
C2.ar: اختيار الكلمة الدقيقة بين المترادفات المتقاربة، مع التحكّم في التلازم والفارق الدلالي.
examples: The findings refute, not merely question, the claim.
a substantial (not 'big') increase
to terminate a contract vs to end a friendship
keen vs eager vs avid

C2.title: Connotation, nuance & evaluative language
C2.en: Control positive/negative/neutral connotation and loaded language to convey precise evaluation: slim vs skinny; assertive vs pushy; frugal vs stingy; a regime vs a government.
C2.ar: التحكّم في الدلالة الإيجابية/السلبية/المحايدة واللغة المحمّلة لنقل تقييم دقيق: slim مقابل skinny؛ assertive مقابل pushy.
examples: 'Frugal' praises; 'stingy' condemns.
'Assertive' vs 'pushy' — same act, different judgement.
a 'regime' vs a 'government'
'childlike' vs 'childish'

C2.title: Idioms, proverbs & fixed expressions (mastery)
C2.en: Understand and deploy a wide range of idioms, proverbs and fixed phrases appropriately, including recognising when to avoid them.
C2.ar: فهم واستخدام طيف واسع من التعابير والأمثال والعبارات الثابتة بشكل مناسب، مع إدراك متى يُتجنّب استخدامها.
examples: to bite the bullet
a stitch in time saves nine
the elephant in the room
to hedge one's bets

C2.title: Allusion, wordplay & figurative extension
C2.en: Recognise and create allusion, puns, extended metaphor and creative figurative language for effect.
C2.ar: إدراك وإنشاء التلميح والتورية والاستعارة الممتدّة واللغة المجازية الإبداعية للأثر.
examples: an Achilles' heel
a play on words in a headline
an extended metaphor of a 'journey'
a biblical/literary allusion

C2.title: Irony, understatement & litotes
C2.en: Convey and interpret irony, understatement, litotes and dry humour, where the intended meaning departs from the literal.
C2.ar: نقل وتفسير السخرية والتهوين والتلطيف بالنفي المزدوج والفكاهة الجافّة، حيث يخالف المعنى المقصود الحرفي.
examples: 'Not bad at all' (= excellent).
'A minor detail' (said of a huge problem).
'I'm not entirely convinced' (= I disagree).
'It's just a scratch' (of major damage).

C2.title: Register mixing & tone control for effect
C2.en: Deliberately blend registers and shift tone for rhetorical, humorous or persuasive effect, fully in control of the audience's response.
C2.ar: المزج المتعمّد بين المستويات اللغوية وتحويل النبرة لأثر بلاغي أو فكاهي أو إقناعي، مع تحكّم كامل في استجابة الجمهور.
examples: dropping a colloquialism into formal prose for effect
mock-formality for humour
a sudden shift to plain speech for impact
elevated diction to signal gravity

C2.title: Rhetoric & persuasion (parallelism, tricolon, antithesis)
C2.en: Structure language for persuasive impact using rhetorical devices: parallelism, tricolon, antithesis, rhetorical questions, anaphora.
C2.ar: بناء اللغة للأثر الإقناعي باستخدام الأدوات البلاغية: التوازي، والثلاثيات، والتضادّ، والأسئلة البلاغية، والتصدير.
examples: We came, we saw, we conquered.
Ask not what your country can do for you…
Not this, but that.
The more we have, the more we want.

C2.title: Sophisticated counter-argument, concession & rebuttal
C2.en: Anticipate, concede and rebut opposing views with nuance: admittedly… nonetheless; while it is true that…; granted that…; this overlooks the fact that…
C2.ar: توقّع الآراء المضادّة والتسليم بها ودحضها بدقّة: admittedly… nonetheless؛ while it is true that…؛ granted that…؛ this overlooks…
examples: Admittedly, costs rise; nonetheless, the gain justifies them.
While it is true that risks exist, they are manageable.
Granted that time is short, quality must not suffer.
This argument overlooks a key fact.

C2.title: Concision, elegance & editing for style
C2.en: Prune redundancy, sharpen phrasing and achieve economy and elegance: cut deadwood, prefer the precise verb, vary sentence length for rhythm.
C2.ar: تقليم الحشو وشحذ الصياغة وتحقيق الاقتصاد والأناقة: حذف الزوائد، وتفضيل الفعل الدقيق، وتنويع طول الجُمَل للإيقاع.
examples: 'due to the fact that' → 'because'
'in the event that' → 'if'
replacing a weak verb + noun with a strong verb
varying long and short sentences for effect

C2.title: Spontaneous fluency, paraphrase & seamless repair
C2.en: Sustain effortless, precise spontaneous speech; paraphrase instantly around any gap and self-repair so smoothly it is barely noticeable.
C2.ar: الحفاظ على كلام عفوي دقيق بلا عناء؛ وإعادة الصياغة فورًا حول أيّ ثغرة، والتصحيح الذاتي بسلاسة لا تكاد تُلاحَظ.
examples: reformulating mid-sentence without a pause
'or rather', 'that is to say', 'to put it differently'
circumlocuting a forgotten word seamlessly
holding the floor with natural fillers

C2.title: Full mastery: flexible, effortless, precise use + capstone review
C2.en: Integrate all C2 resources — marked syntax, nuance, register, rhetoric, idiom — into effortless, precise, stylistically controlled communication; consolidate all C2.
C2.ar: دمج كل موارد C2 — التركيب المميّز، والدلالة الدقيقة، والأسلوب، والبلاغة، والتعابير — في تواصل دقيق وسلس ومضبوط أسلوبيًا؛ ومراجعة كل C2.
examples: shifting register mid-speech with full control
combining cleft, inversion and nuance in one argument
sustaining a precise, elegant extended discourse
adapting instantly to audience and purpose
